title: Finite locally free projective bundles and tautological base change
statement:
Let $B$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $n\geq0$, and $F$ a locally free $\mathcal O_B$-module of constant rank $n+1$ [def-amb-finite-locally-free-module]. Put $P=\operatorname{Proj}_B(\operatorname{Sym}^{\bullet}F)$ with projection $p:P\to B$, using the symmetric algebra sheaf [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-symmetric-algebra] with the symmetric grading [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-graded] and relative Proj [def-nagata-relative-proj]. The degree-one twisting module $\mathcal O_P(1)$, obtained on each affine base open from the shifted graded module [def-weil-pbc-proj-twisting-sheaf] $\operatorname{Sym}^{\bullet}(F)(1)$ and glued by homogeneous localization, is invertible [def-sc-invertible-module]. The morphism $p$ is proper [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Every frame of $F|_U$ identifies $(P|_U,\mathcal O_P(1)|_{P|_U})$ with $(\mathbf P^n_U,\mathcal O(1))$, where projective space is [def-nagata-relative-projective-space] and its twist has transition functions $e_i=(T_i/T_j)e_j$ [def-pc-projective-space-twist]. For any scheme morphism $g:B'\to B$, there is a canonical isomorphism
$$\mathbf P_{B'}(g^*F)\cong B'\times_B P$$
carrying its degree-one twisting module to the pullback of $\mathcal O_P(1)$. These isomorphisms respect identities and composition. On $\mathbf P^n_K$ over any field $K$, with coordinates $T_0,\ldots,T_n$ and $n\geq1$, the subscheme $T_0=0$ is $\mathbf P^{n-1}_K$, its complement is $\mathbf A^n_K$ with coordinates $t_i=T_i/T_0$, and each divisor $T_i=0$ has associated line bundle $\mathcal O(1)$. The intersection $T_1=\cdots=T_n=0$ is the reduced point $[1:0:\cdots:0]$ in that affine chart. For $n=0$, $p$ is an isomorphism and $\mathcal O_P(1)$ corresponds to $F$.

source.place: Tag 01OB, label definition-projective-bundle; Tag 01O3, label lemma-relative-proj-base-change (including theta on twists); Tag 01OE, label lemma-projective-space-bundle; properness from local projective space

proof.text: Choose a Zariski cover trivializing $F$ and refine it by affine opens $V=\operatorname{Spec}R$, using [def-amb-finite-locally-free-module]. In a chosen frame $v_0,\ldots,v_n$, [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-symmetric-algebra] identifies the affine sections of $\operatorname{Sym}F$ with $\operatorname{Sym}_R(R^{n+1})$. By [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-free-module-polynomial], the map sending $v_i$ to $T_i$ is an algebra isomorphism with $R[T_0,\ldots,T_n]$. It is graded: [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-graded] describes degree $d$ as the span of products of $d$ degree-one generators, and the map and its inverse send each such product to a product of the same length. The same construction works for a frame on any open $U$, since its affine restrictions agree on their degree-one generators and hence agree as maps of symmetric algebra sheaves.

source.place: Tag 01OB, definition-projective-bundle; Tag 01OE, lemma-projective-space-bundle, polynomial symmetric algebra

proof.text: Apply the graded-equivalence clause of [prop-nagata-relative-proj-functoriality] to the frame isomorphism in step 1. Relative Proj and its affine restriction data [def-nagata-relative-proj] then identify $P|_U$ with $\operatorname{Proj}_U\operatorname{Sym}(\mathcal O_U^{n+1})=\mathbf P^n_U$ [def-nagata-relative-projective-space]. On an affine base piece, $D_+(T_i)$ has structure ring $H_i=(R[T_0,\ldots,T_n])_{(T_i),0}$, and these opens cover, by [prop-nagata-proj-standard-open], since the variables generate the positive-degree ideal. This proves the scheme part of the assertion about every frame, not just about the frames in the initial covering.

Here is the compatibility needed to glue the affine twists. For a degree-preserving algebra isomorphism $\alpha:A\to C$, the map on the degree-one localization modules is $a/f^m\mapsto\alpha(a)/\alpha(f)^m$, with $\deg a=m\deg f+1$; its inverse is the same formula for $\alpha^{-1}$. The fraction relation is preserved by a ring map, and the formula commutes with the localization restriction maps in [def-weil-pbc-proj-twisting-sheaf]. For restriction on the base, use that same formula with the coefficient restriction map on a principal affine refinement, as in the overlap data of [def-nagata-relative-proj]. For a principal base restriction $R\to R_s$, on a frame chart both restrictions are the free module $H_i[1/s]T_i$: multiplication by $T_i$ identifies the degree-one fractions with the degree-zero ring, with inverse division by $T_i$. Thus restrictions and frame changes induce compatible isomorphisms of the local twisting modules. The identity and triple-overlap equations follow by applying the composite algebra map to the numerator and denominator. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-site-module-sheaf-gluing] on the Zariski open site of $P$ to these overlap isomorphisms to obtain the global module $L$. Its affine identifications are precisely $\widetilde{(\operatorname{Sym}F)(1)}$; thus $L$ is the twisting module $\mathcal O_P(1)$ specified in the statement. No intersection of affine base opens is assumed affine: the formulas are checked on principal refinements inside affine pieces, and then on an affine covering of each overlap.

source.place: Tag 01NR, lemma-glue-relative-proj-twists (explicit localization cocycle); Tag 01MN, definition-twist; Tag 04TR, sites-lemma-glue-sheaves

proof.text: On a frame chart $D_+(T_i)$, the definition of the shift in [def-weil-pbc-proj-twisting-sheaf] gives $L=(A_{T_i})_1$, where $A=R[T_0,\ldots,T_n]$. Multiplication by $T_i$ gives an $H_i$-linear isomorphism $H_i\to(A_{T_i})_1$, with inverse $a/T_i^m\mapsto a/T_i^{m+1}$; the two composites are the identity by multiplication of fractions. On an overlap the generators satisfy $T_i=(T_i/T_j)T_j$. Hence $L$ is locally free of rank one, so invertible by [def-sc-invertible-module], and these trivializations identify it with [def-pc-projective-space-twist] by $e_i\mapsto T_i$. The maps agree on overlaps by the displayed identity; they and their inverses glue by applying the sheaf axiom to local sections. Together with step 2 this proves the asserted identification of pairs in every frame.

source.place: Tag 01MS, lemma-when-invertible, proof with d=1; Tag 01OB

proof.text: To use properness for the precise projective-space interface, apply [lemma-nagata-relative-proj-base-change-arbitrary] to $\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}[T_0,\ldots,T_n]$ and $U\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$. The pullback algebra is $\mathcal O_U[T_0,\ldots,T_n]$: on each affine piece this is [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-base-change] applied to the free module, with the polynomial identification of step 1. Thus $\mathbf P^n_U$ of step 2 is canonically $\mathbf P(\{0,\ldots,n\};U)$ of [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change], over $U$. This latter structural morphism is proper by [lemma-nagata-projective-space-base-change-proper]. Therefore $p$ is proper over every member of the frame cover, and [lemma-nagata-projective-target-local] gives properness over $B$. These results require no Noetherian, finite-type-base, or separated-base hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 01OE, lemma-projective-space-bundle; Tag 01O3, lemma-relative-proj-base-change; Tag 01NH, lemma-projective-space-separated; properness and its target locality are the cited existing nodes (Morphisms Tag 01W2, lemma-proper-local-on-the-base)

proof.text:
Let $g:B'\to B$ be arbitrary. The pullback of $F$ is quasi-coherent by [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-quasi-coherent], and its affine sections on $W=\operatorname{Spec}S\subseteq g^{-1}(\operatorname{Spec}R)$ are $S\otimes_R F(\operatorname{Spec}R)$ by [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-affine-sections] (interchanging the tensor factors). Apply [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-base-change] to obtain an isomorphism
$$S\otimes_R\operatorname{Sym}_R F(\operatorname{Spec}R)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Sym}_S(S\otimes_R F(\operatorname{Spec}R)).$$
It sends $s\otimes\iota(v)$ to $s\iota(1\otimes v)$. It and its inverse preserve degree, since the homogeneous pieces are the spans of products of degree-one generators [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-graded]. These maps agree under restriction: both restriction composites agree on coefficients and on every $\iota(v)$, hence on all products and sums. By the sheaf axiom they give a canonical graded algebra isomorphism $g^*\operatorname{Sym}F\cong\operatorname{Sym}(g^*F)$. The affine-section identifications here are those of [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-symmetric-algebra].

source.place: Tag 01O3, lemma-relative-proj-base-change, applied to Sym F; Algebra Tag 0C6F, lemma-tensor-algebra-localization (general scalar extension by the symmetric universal property); Schemes Tag 01I9, lemma-widetilde-pullback

proof.text: Apply [lemma-nagata-relative-proj-base-change-arbitrary] to $\operatorname{Sym}F$ and the graded-equivalence clause of [prop-nagata-relative-proj-functoriality] to step 6. This constructs the asserted isomorphism $\mathbf P_{B'}(g^*F)\cong B'\times_B P$. To fix its map, use [lem-nagata-affine-proj-scalar-extension] on the affine pieces in step 6. If $\beta$ is that graded scalar-extension isomorphism and $\psi(a)=\beta(1\otimes a)$, the map to $P$ has inverse image $D_+(\psi(f))$ of $D_+(f)$ and ring map $a/f^m\mapsto\psi(a)/\psi(f)^m$. These formulas determine the map uniquely on the covering by the pulled-back frame charts; in particular this is the canonical coefficient-pullback comparison, with no flatness condition on $g$.

Let $r:\mathbf P_{B'}(g^*F)\to P$ be the projection just constructed. On a pulled-back frame chart the modules in $r^*L\to L'$ are free of rank one by step 4; define the map by $r^*T_i\mapsto T'_i=\psi(T_i)$. In affine module coordinates this is an isomorphism: pullback of $H_iT_i$ is $H'_i\otimes_{H_i}H_iT_i\cong H'_iT'_i$, by [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-affine-sections]. The ring map of step 7 sends $T_i/T_j$ to $T'_i/T'_j$, so these maps agree on overlaps of standard charts. Across changes of base frame, they too agree: on a degree-one fraction both formulas send $a/f^m$ to $\psi(a)/\psi(f)^m$, using step 3 and the map on generators in step 6. Thus maps and inverses glue by the sheaf axiom. This proves the canonical isomorphism $r^*\mathcal O_P(1)\cong\mathcal O_{\mathbf P_{B'}(g^*F)}(1)$; it gives exactly the degree-one part of the twist comparison, rather than assuming that part from the scheme-only base-change node. The meaning of pullback is [def-pc-module-pullback], and the fraction description is [def-weil-pbc-proj-twisting-sheaf].

source.place: Tag 01O3, lemma-relative-proj-base-change, theta; Tag 01N2, lemma-base-change-map-proj, twist comparison made explicit in rank-one frame charts

proof.text: For the identity base map the maps in steps 6--8 fix coefficients, degree-one generators, and all fractions. For $B''\xrightarrow{h}B'\xrightarrow{g}B$, identify the iterated module pullbacks by [def-pc-module-pullback]. On affine pieces with coefficient maps $R\to S\to T$, both symmetric-algebra maps send $t\otimes(s\otimes\iota(v))$ to $t\,\overline{s}\,\iota(1\otimes v)$; the corresponding maps on every Proj chart send $a/f^m$ to its image over $T$. By the uniqueness of the chart-described morphism in [lem-nagata-affine-proj-scalar-extension] and [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing], the comparison scheme maps coincide. Their maps into the fibre products coincide by the two projections [def-pc-fibre-product]. On the line modules both composites carry the pulled-back generator $T_i$ to the same generator over $T$, so they coincide as well. This proves identity and composition compatibility for both the scheme and twist isomorphisms.

source.place: Tag 01O3 and Tag 01N2, coefficient maps on homogeneous fractions; composition checked explicitly

proof.text: Now let $K$ be any field and $n\geq1$. The quotient $K[T_0,\ldots,T_n]\twoheadrightarrow K[T_1,\ldots,T_n]$, setting $T_0=0$, is graded and surjective. The closed-immersion clause of [prop-nagata-relative-proj-functoriality] gives $\mathbf P^{n-1}_K\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^n_K$, using [def-nagata-relative-projective-space] over the affine base. On $D_+(T_j)$ for $j\ne0$, the map on dehomogenized rings sets $T_0/T_j$ equal to zero and fixes all other coordinates [lem-weil-pbc-dehomogenization-polynomial-ring]. Its kernel is $(T_0/T_j)$: expand a polynomial in that one variable as its constant term plus that variable times a polynomial. The source has no $D_+(T_0)$ chart. Thus this immersion is scheme-theoretically the subscheme $T_0=0$, not just a bijection on points. Its twist restricts to the lower-dimensional twist, since the local generators $T_j$ and ratios $T_j/T_k$ restrict to the identically named ones, as in step 4.

source.place: Tag 01OE and Tag 01NG; coordinate quotient with the closed-immersion property of Proj

proof.text: The complement of $T_0=0$ is $D_+(T_0)$: in its local trivialization the section $T_0$ vanishes exactly where its coefficient is in the point's maximal ideal. By [lem-weil-pbc-projective-space-standard-charts], its non-vanishing locus is the standard open, and that chart has coordinate algebra $K[t_1,\ldots,t_n]$, $t_i=T_i/T_0$. By [def-sbc-affine-space], this chart is $\mathbf A^n_K$. The base-change model used by that chart theorem is the same one identified with relative Proj in step 5, with the same generators by steps 4 and 8.

For any $i$, the equation of $D_i=\{T_i=0\}$ on $U_j=D_+(T_j)$ is $q_j=T_i/T_j$, by [lem-weil-pbc-projective-space-standard-charts]. For $j=i$ this is $1$; for $j\ne i$ it is one polynomial variable, a nonzerodivisor because multiplying by it shifts the monomial coefficients injectively. Hence the ideal is an effective Cartier ideal [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal]. Its associated line bundle is the dual ideal [def-pc-divisor-line-bundle]. Let $h_j$ be the dual generator with $h_j(q_j)=1$. On $U_j\cap U_k$ one has $q_k=(T_j/T_k)q_j$, hence $h_j=(T_j/T_k)h_k$. These are exactly the transitions for $\mathcal O(1)$ in [def-pc-projective-space-twist], so $e_j\mapsto h_j$ glues to $\mathcal O(1)\cong\mathcal O(D_i)$. This also checks the sign of the twist: it is $+1$.

source.place: Tag 01WR, definition-effective-Cartier-divisor; Tag 01WX, definition-invertible-sheaf-effective-Cartier-divisor; coordinate charts from Constructions Tag 01NG, lemma-standard-covering-projective-space

proof.text: The scheme-theoretic intersection $T_1=\cdots=T_n=0$ has empty intersection with $D_+(T_i)$ for $i\geq1$, because there the defining ideal contains $T_i/T_i=1$. By the covering and coordinate-ring clauses of [lem-weil-pbc-projective-space-standard-charts], it is therefore entirely in $D_+(T_0)=\mathbf A^n_K$, where its coordinate ring is $K[t_1,\ldots,t_n]/(t_1,\ldots,t_n)\cong K$ (evaluation at zero, with inverse the constants). This is a reduced point, with coordinates $t_1=\cdots=t_n=0$, hence the homogeneous point $[1:0:\cdots:0]$. In particular no nilpotent thickening is hidden in the assertion about the intersection.

source.place: Tag 01NG, standard affine coordinates, explicit quotient ideal computation

proof.text: Finally take $n=0$. Over any framed affine base open, the positive-degree ideal of $R[T]$ is generated by $T$, so its entire Proj is $D_+(T)$ by [prop-nagata-proj-standard-open]. By [lem-weil-pbc-dehomogenization-polynomial-ring] its degree-zero localization is the polynomial ring on zero variables, namely $R$, with structure map the identity. Thus $p$ is locally an isomorphism to the base; the local inverses agree because each is an inverse to $p$ on its open, and glue by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing]. Moreover, step 4 identifies the twist with the free module generated by $T$. The local isomorphism $F\to L$ over this base identification sends the frame $v$ to $T$. If $v'=uv$ for a unit $u$, then $T'=uT$ by the degree-one symmetric algebra map, so this isomorphism is independent of the frame and glues. Hence $\mathcal O_P(1)$ corresponds to $F$, including when $F$ is a nontrivial line bundle. All covering arguments also apply to the empty base.
